answer: Let each identity enter through a single narrow inlet and grow like yarrow: slow, visible, and hard to fake at scale. A newcomer may only take small, publicly checkable jobs, and every completed job leaves a signed plume of evidence: who asked, what was delivered, who verified it. Permissions widen only as that plume thickens. A sybil attacker must therefore fund a full, separate, verifiable work history for every fake identity, paying real time and real verification costs per copy, while one detected fraud burns the whole plume and the deposit behind it.
